subject: environmental-science
title: Bioremediation and Phytoremediation
welcome_lead: Plants and microbes as nature's cleanup crew for contaminated land.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on heavy metals, plastics and biological remediation.
final_note: Mitigation is cheapest at source — but biology can finish what engineering leaves behind.

concepts.def: Use of microorganisms to break down pollutants in soil or water.
Use of plants to remove, stabilise or degrade contaminants.
Plants accumulate metals in shoots, then harvested (e.g., Brassica with Ni).
Plants immobilise contaminants in roots/rhizosphere, reducing leaching.
Plastic particle <5 mm; widespread in marine and freshwater systems.
High-density metal (Pb, Cd, Hg, As) toxic at low concentrations; bioaccumulative.

walkthroughs.body_html: Pseudomonas spp. degrade hydrocarbons aerobically; Dehalococcoides dechlorinate solvents anaerobically. Conditions and nutrients are tuned to favour target metabolism.
Alpine pennycress (Thlaspi caerulescens) accumulates Zn and Cd to ~3% dry mass — orders above normal plants.
Microplastics enter food webs via filter feeders, transferring sorbed POPs. UV photodegradation produces nanoplastics that cross biological membranes.

Less than 5 μm in diameter
Larger than 1 cm
Visible only by SEM

mcqs.q: How does fertiliser runoff cause aquatic dead zones?
options: Excess nutrients fuel algal blooms; when algae die, decomposition depletes water oxygen.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Fertiliser directly poisons fish.

mcqs.q: Why are top predators most affected by persistent pollutants like mercury?
options: Biomagnification concentrates pollutants at each trophic level up the food chain.
Predators are exposed to more pollution directly.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Bacteria produce them.

mcqs.q: How are most microplastics formed in the environment?
options: Predators have weaker immune systems.
Larger plastic items break down physically into smaller fragments over time.
Bacteria produce them.
They are all manufactured at microscopic size deliberately.
